decisions.reason: As a standalone thermal inkjet launch close to the core portfolio, it benefits from sunk development and sales investments and management can still justify patience in a growing market as adoption ramps up.
Despite possible overlap with other inkjet offers, its close fit with the firm's in-house R&D-based identification business makes management more likely to persist than to admit an early misstep.
This flagship industrial laser line is highly visible and central to the firm's announced Industry 4.0 direction, so escalation of commitment strongly favors continued support.
The newly launched laser cabin extends the firm's established laser offering and, with only one year in market, any shortfall can readily be framed as temporary rather than grounds for withdrawal.
Although more specialized, the lubricant printing system builds on the firm's coding competence and its trade-fair award gives management a credible basis to continue backing it rather than retreat.
